mechanism_of_action.value: Synthetic, beta-1 selective (cardioselective) adrenoceptor blocking agent without significant membrane stabilizing activity or intrinsic sympathomimetic activity in its therapeutic dosage range; at higher doses (>= 20 mg) it also inhibits beta-2 adrenoceptors. Antihypertensive mechanisms may include decreased cardiac output, inhibition of renal renin release, and diminution of tonic sympathetic outflow.

tier.note: No adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Animal studies showed no teratogenicity up to high multiples of MRHD, but fetotoxicity (increased late resorptions in rats at 50 mg/kg/day) and embryolethality (increased early resorptions in rabbits at 12.5 mg/kg/day) occurred. Label advises use during pregnancy only if potential benefit justifies potential risk to the fetus.

refs.quote: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Bisoprolol fumarate tablets should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
Bisoprolol fumarate was fetotoxic (increased late resorptions) at 50 mg/kg/day and maternotoxic (decreased food intake and body weight gain) at 150 mg/kg/day.

refs.quote: Small amounts of bisoprolol fumarate (< 2% of the dose) have been detected in the milk of lactating rats. It is not known whether this drug is excreted in human milk.
